items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Our group was known as Drum Boogie number 789. We arrived in Honolulu the next day and Bubbles Martin was not feeling well... the troupe could not go or leave one of its members behind.

ctx.x: 14 and a half hours before landing at Hickam field. We didn't have anything to drink other than water because alchohol was not allowed on the air base or military planes, but we played black jack and visited the pilot's cabins. That night we ran into some stormy weather which had the plane flying in most every position except upside down, and the only person that became air sick was the hostess.

Every U.S.O. unit had a number and name. Our group was known as Drum Boogie number 789. We arrived in Honolulu the next day and Bubbles Martin was not feeling well, and went to see a doctor at the Hickam Field Base Hospital. He was put in bed and we were told that we could have passes to go into the city. That was quite alright with me because I had heard so much about Honolulu's Hawaii and wanted to see what it was like, although I didn't expect to see the chicks in grass skirts and I didn't see any. We had no…

We were given a pass every day and the second night, we found a dance hall that had some jazz musicians playing there. The next night we had our instruments and jammed until the joint closed. There was an alto player with the band that looked exactly like a musician named Durante whom I had seen at the Savoy ballroom with an orchestra known as the San Domingo Serenaders and he played exactly the same style.
